canon_requests.section: Canon §4.4 (doc 03 Canon gaps G29, door and trapdoor panels)
canon_requests.old: Opacity and sound attenuation of a cell scale with its fill fraction below 48 micro-voxels (literal fill rule, no door exception).
canon_requests.new: A closed door or closed trapdoor applies its block's full `light_filter`, concealment and sound attenuation.
canon_requests.why: A closed panel fills 16 micro-voxels, so under the literal fill rule a closed oak door filters 3 light levels and attenuates 43 of its 175 ddB; light and sound would leak through shut doors. Chapter 03 §4.4 adopted this wording ahead of canon in wave 2 (closed panels read registry `light_filter`, `conceal`, `sound_atten_ddb` unscaled; §11.2, §11.5 and acceptance 25, 53 updated), so the canon must carry it or the chapter must revert.

canon_requests.section: Canon §4.4 (doc 03 Canon gaps G30, shapes without micro-voxels)
canon_requests.old: Fill scaling applies to every shape, so cross, ladder and fixture cells (empty predefined mask) would read concealment 0.
canon_requests.new: Shapes with no micro-voxels (cross, ladder, fixture) keep their block's light filter, concealment and sound attenuation unscaled.
canon_requests.why: Canon §12.2 gives tall grass concealment 2 and leaves 3; a literal fill rule would zero them. Chapter 03 §4.4 keeps registry values for the four empty-mask shapes (none, ladder, cross, fixture).

canon_requests.section: Canon §4.2 Movement (doc 03 Canon gaps G31 part 1; DECISIONS 95 ledge mantle)
canon_requests.old: canon-1.11 §4.2 has no mantle line; the chapter used h in (550, 1600] mm measured from the feet at the press.
canon_requests.new: Ledge mantle: a JUMP press with forward input, or a grappling arrival with forward input, mantles onto a ledge whose top lies more than 550 mm and at most 2,000 mm above the feet and at most 2,000 mm above the feet's height at the end of the body's last grounded, swimming, climbing or grappling tick (`ledge_base_y`). A jump adds no reach: from a floor the highest mantle is 2,000 mm (two blocks) at every VERVE. Fences and panes are never mantle targets. The crouched capsule needs free space to `land_y + 1,201 mm`.
canon_requests.why: DECISIONS 95 names doc 03 for a 2,000 mm mantle; the chapter adopted this rule in §5.9 (ledges 750..2000 mm take 16..28 ticks; 2,250 mm fails with or without a jump) and §5.1 (`ledge_base_y`). The product question whether 2,000 mm includes the jump was settled by default as measured from `ledge_base_y`; the canon must state it, since the alternative (3,100 mm with a jump) changes doc 12's 2-block climb rule (doc 12 §1, §15.1, §18.1).

canon_requests.section: Canon §4.2 Movement (doc 03 Canon gaps G31 part 1; DECISIONS 95 sprint-slide)
canon_requests.new: Sprint-slide (base kit, no new input): a CROUCH press while sprinting on the ground with forward input at a horizontal speed of at least 5,000 mm/s, at most once per 60 ticks, starts a slide at max(current speed, 8,000 mm/s) along the current horizontal direction. The body holds crouch height, ignores the input axes and status multipliers, and decelerates by 8,000 mm/s² × ground `friction_bp`. The slide ends after 45 ticks, when its speed along the slide direction drops to 2,000 mm/s or below, when the body leaves the ground, on a movement gate or downed, or on a JUMP press (which keeps the horizontal velocity for a ground jump or a mantle). A slide costs no stamina and emits sprint-gait footsteps. On friction 10,000 a slide from 6,500 mm/s covers 3,799 mm in 45 ticks; on ice (1,500) 5,669 mm.
canon_requests.why: DECISIONS 95 names a sprint-slide with no numbers in any chapter; doc 03 §5.23 defined the motion, doc 17 binds it to `input.crouch` while sprinting and doc 09 rates its noise. The canon should carry the numbers so that docs 04, 05, 09, 16 and 17 bind to one source.

canon_requests.section: Canon §4.2 Movement and §13.1 Item categories (doc 03 Canon gaps G31 part 1; DECISIONS 95 grappling tool)
canon_requests.new: Grappling tool: an item (`cat.tool`, genre-skinned, with a cooldown owned by doc 11), never part of the base kit, used from the quickbar as an item-use action. A use casts a 20,000 mm ray from the eye along the aim; it anchors on any block face (fixed terrain included) at least 1,000 mm away, else the use is refused and spends nothing. A pull moves the body at 12,000 mm/s toward the anchor with no gravity for at most 120 ticks; it releases on a JUMP press (velocity kept; the mantle test runs), on arrival within 1,000 mm, when the body stops gaining on the anchor, on a movement gate or downed, or when the anchor block is gone (velocity × 0.25 in these cases). An arrival with forward input or a JUMP press may mantle onto a ledge within 2,000 mm of the body's feet height during the pull. A body is never an anchor.
canon_requests.why: DECISIONS 95 puts the grappling tool in the game as an item and names docs 03, 05, 11 and 17; doc 03 §5.24 defined `start_grapple` and the pull, doc 11 must define the item, doc 05 its action slot. Canon §13.1 should list the tool so the item is content, not a base verb.

canon_requests.section: Canon new §5.12 Folio climate (doc 03 Canon gaps G31 part 2; DECISIONS 99; the same table that doc 09 G26 requests as a new Canon §12.4 and doc 12 G19 proposes under Canon §5.9 and §12)
canon_requests.new: Each Folio has one time of day and one weather state, drawn by worldgen from its genre's tables and fixed for the Folio. Time of day: `tod.dawn` sky_delta −1, `tod.day` 0, `tod.dusk` −1, `tod.night` −3. Weather: `wx.clear` (sky_delta 0, sound_ddb 0, precip none, fire_bp 10000), `wx.rain` (−1, 2, water, 5000), `wx.storm` (−2, 4, water, 2500), `wx.fog` (−1, 0, none, 10000), `wx.snow` (−1, 2, none, 5000), `wx.dust` (−1, 3, none, 12500). Terms: a sky-lit sky source adds sky_delta(tod) + sky_delta(wx) to its level, clamped to 0..15; a sound propagation step into a sky-open cell costs sound_ddb(wx) more; under precipitation every body whose body-contact cell is sky-open gains `st.soaked` on each status pulse; fire spread into a sky-open cell is multiplied by fire_bp(wx). Weather deposits no liquid or gas and changes no temperature; any cell under a micro-voxel is sheltered from every term except light. The table also carries the stealth columns doc 09 §15.3 reads (fog points, sound_bp, ambient_db, precip, snow) and the presentation columns doc 18 reads (fog, ambient sound).
canon_requests.why: DECISIONS 99 names doc 03 and canon-1.11 carries nothing; doc 03 §4.8 adopted these IDs and terms ahead of canon and wired them into §6.10, §8.3, §10.2, §11.2, §11.4, §16.1 and the Exports. Three chapters (03, 09, 12) request the same table under three different canon section numbers with different columns; one canon section must merge them.

canon_requests.section: Canon §17.6 Ghosts (doc 03 Canon gaps G6, never triaged)
canon_requests.new: A ghost has no body collision and is excluded from hit, push and perception queries; voxel collision stays, so a ghost cannot leave the Folio. Ghosts toggle doors and never place or break blocks.
canon_requests.why: G6 is the chapter's reading since the first draft and was never triaged; without it a literal reading lets ghosts fall through the floor or leave the Folio box.

canon_requests.section: Canon §4.4 Destruction (doc 03 verify:03 reading, no gap filed)
canon_requests.new: Destruction removes micro-voxels, not whole cells, from shapes that chip (full, pillar, slab, stairs, layer). Door, trapdoor, ladder, fence, pane, cross and fixture cells and resource nodes break whole, and a cell an explosion's rays mark breaks whole.
canon_requests.why: Docs 03 §13.2 and 07 §10.8 break the listed shapes whole and explosions break marked cells whole; the wave-2 verifier judged this an acceptable reading and filed nothing, so the canon's absolute sentence still contradicts both chapters on its face.

product_questions.question: DECISIONS 95's "ledge mantle up to 2,000 mm": is the 2,000 mm measured from the feet at the moment of the press (so a jump first adds its apex, up to 3,100 mm, three blocks) or from the floor the body last stood on?
product_questions.default_applied: From the floor: §5.9 mantles a ledge at most 2,000 mm above `ledge_base_y` (feet height at the end of the last grounded, swimming, climbing or grappling tick) and at most 2,000 mm above the current feet; a jump adds no reach, so two blocks is the ceiling at every VERVE and doc 12's 2-block pit and climb rules hold without a jump.
options: From the floor via `ledge_base_y` (applied; two blocks max, doc 12 unchanged)
From the feet at the press (jump adds reach; three-block walls climbable; doc 12 §1, §15.1, §18.1 and worldgen reachability change)
A per-genre or per-VERVE mantle height

product_questions.question: Sprint-slide numbers (no chapter had any): entry speed, start speed, deceleration, cap, cooldown, stamina cost?
product_questions.default_applied: Entry at ≥ 5,000 mm/s horizontal while sprinting on the ground with forward input and `stance_base = i32::MAX`; start speed max(current, 8,000 mm/s); deceleration 8,000 mm/s² × ground `friction_bp`; ends after 45 ticks, below 2,000 mm/s along the slide direction, when airborne, on a gate or downed, or on a JUMP press; 60-tick cooldown; no stamina cost; crouch height held; sprint-gait footsteps. 3,799 mm on friction 10000 from a 6,500 mm/s sprint, 5,669 mm on ice.
options: Keep the §5.23 numbers (applied)
Shorter, cheaper slide (e.g. 30-tick cap, start at current speed) for stealth genres
Stamina cost on start (doc 04 owns it)

product_questions.question: Grappling tool numbers and anchoring: ray length, pull speed, duration cap, arrival radius, release velocity, and may it anchor on fixed terrain and ceilings?
product_questions.default_applied: 20,000 mm ray from the eye; anchors on any block face (fixed terrain included) at least 1,000 mm away; 12,000 mm/s pull with no gravity for at most 120 ticks; release on JUMP (velocity kept, mantle test runs), on arrival within 1,000 mm, when blocked, gated, downed or when the anchor block is gone (velocity × 0.25); a body is never an anchor; the pull resets `peak_y`, so no fall damage accrues during it; doc 11 owns cooldown and skins.
options: Keep the §5.24 numbers (applied)
Shorter line (e.g. 12 m) and slower pull to keep doc 12's vertical gating meaningful
Allow entity anchors (pull enemies or be pulled), which doc 05 §19.3 grapple rules would then share

product_questions.question: DECISIONS 99 climate: which time-of-day and weather states exist, and which simulation terms do they feed?
product_questions.default_applied: Four times of day (`tod.dawn|day|dusk|night`, sky deltas −1/0/−1/−3) and six weathers (`wx.clear|rain|storm|fog|snow|dust`) with sky_delta, sound_ddb, precip and fire_bp columns (§4.8); light, sound, surfaces (`st.soaked` under rain or storm when sky-open) and fire spread are affected; weather deposits no liquid or gas and changes no temperature; roofed cells see only the light term. Doc 12 rolls both per Folio and calls `set_climate` before the light bake.
options: Keep §4.8's six weathers and four times of day as the canon-1.12 table (applied), merged with doc 09's stealth columns and doc 18's presentation columns
Weather also deposits water (puddles) and lowers temperature under snow, which touches §6, §9 and doc 08
Weather changes over the Folio's life (fronts), which doc 12's `gpv.evt.weather_front` already covers as an event

product_questions.question: G29: should closed doors and trapdoors block light and sound fully, against Canon §4.4's literal fill rule?
product_questions.default_applied: Yes, adopted ahead of canon in §4.4: a closed panel applies registry `light_filter`, `conceal` and `sound_atten_ddb` unscaled (oak door 15 and 175 ddB closed, 3 and 43 open); the Canon gaps G29 entry still describes the pre-adoption leak and needs rewording.

product_questions.question: G30: do cross, ladder and fixture cells keep their registry concealment, light filter and sound attenuation although they have no micro-voxels?
product_questions.default_applied: Yes (§4.4): the four empty-mask shapes are not geometry and keep registry values, so tall grass 2 and leaves 3 hold.

Scale to 0 per the literal fill rule and move foliage concealment to doc 09

product_questions.question: Doc 04 §13 says `body.amorphous` and `body.insectoid` climb any solid face; how does the controller do it?
product_questions.default_applied: `BodyState` flag 8 `CLIMB_ANY` (§3.4): every collision box overlapping the capsule AABB expanded by 100 mm counts as climbable (enter between `p.y + STEP_UP` and `p.y + h`, stay between `p.y` and `p.y + h`), at the plan's climb speed; doc 04 sets it on those Errata, doc 13 only on creatures whose navigation uses wall climbing.

product_questions.question: Canon §4.4 says destruction removes micro-voxels, not whole cells; do panel shapes and explosion-marked cells break whole?
product_questions.default_applied: Yes: door, trapdoor, ladder, fence, pane, cross and fixture cells and resource nodes never chip and break whole; explosions break the cells their rays mark whole (§12.2, §13.2); judged a compatible reading, canon clarification proposed.

Chip panels too (16-voxel masks) and let explosions chip marked cells by their ray power

product_questions.question: Homing (ghostline) target rule: which targets qualify and how often is the target re-chosen?
product_questions.default_applied: Live non-ghost bodies carrying `st.marked`, of a faction other than the owner's, within 30,000 mm and 60° of the velocity, best alignment wins (ties to lower EntityId), re-chosen every normal step; the turn budget is the Canon §2.3 accumulator at `home_bam_s` with k = 60 (273 or 274 Bam at 16384); catch-up steps never turn; pitch clamped to ±16000.
options: Keep the §5.19 rule (applied)
Lock at launch (doc 06's glyph.mod.homing model), which doc 06 needs anyway
Home on any hostile, not only `st.marked` (changes ghostline's identity in doc 11)

product_questions.question: DECISIONS 94 ink gore: does the gore toggle change any simulated state?
product_questions.default_applied: No (§4.6): `liq.blood` and every bleed liquid keep their IDs, records and grid behaviour; each viewer's renderer draws them as ink (default), red blood or nothing, so peers with different settings simulate identically.
options: Presentation only (applied)
A distinct `liq.ink` with its own surface rows, which would make the toggle affect simulation and break lockstep
